rows: Distributors involved in Alani Nu transition
Q3 framed as another pivotal quarter in a transformational year - Alani Nu acquisition, PepsiCo captaincy, Rockstar acquisition, leadership additions.
Celsius brand returned to double-digit retail sales growth (13% scanner) after a slow Q1/Q2; 44% reported growth lapped a depressed prior-year inventory-optimization base.
Reported-vs-scanner gap (44% vs 13%) attributed to year-over-year inventory movements; management conceded not a perfect one-to-one comparison and pointed to scanner as the health barometer.
Alani Nu grew triple digits (115% retail, 99% revenue) led by record Witch's Brew sell-through (5th year, more than doubled prior year) plus organic core-SKU growth.
Combined portfolio at 20%+ US energy-category share, grew 31% in tracked channels (~2x category), crossed $5B trailing-52-week US tracked retail sales.
December 1 Alani Nu DSD transition into PepsiCo called a meaningful near-term catalyst; phased load-in means most financial benefit lands in Q1 2026.
Q4 explicitly flagged as a noisy quarter - scrap, freight, returns, secondary warehousing, year-end CPG cash management, plus escalating tariffs; gross margin pressure before re-expanding Q1 2026.
Management declined to size the Q4 net revenue direction; a net drag from returns coming in faster than pipeline refill is 'a scenario that plays out' but unquantified.
~$247M distributor termination expenses recorded in Q3 - fully funded by PepsiCo, deferred and amortized into gross sales, making the transaction cash-neutral.
Rockstar (US + Canada) acquired end of August - ~$11M revenue plus ~$7M GAAP other income (~$18M combined); accounting treatment continues through Q4, normalizes in 2026.
Capital discipline: post-quarter $200M debt paydown and 75 bps rate cut bring total debt to ~$700M, reducing 2026 interest expense ~$20M.
Tariffs escalating - slight in Q2, more in Q3, expected larger in Q4; Midwest premium also a headwind, partly offset by scale, synergies and vertical integration.
Company does not do long-term hedging (only some forward buys) but evaluating it as purchasing power grows; second copacker line coming in 2026.
Pricing under active evaluation given Monster's announced ~5%+ pricing - contemplating frontline price and promotional strategies, building a revenue-management team, but no announcement.
Celsius launched its first-ever LTO, Spritz Vibe, in October (US, Canada, Nordics); robust 2026 innovation slate teased across Celsius and Alani Nu.
Winter Wonderland LTO expected smaller than Witch's Brew, and crossing the distribution transition will not reach full potential this year.
International a growth driver for years to come - first president of international expansion hired; leaning in with strategic 2026 investments; Australia the most successful early market.
Tone confident on strategy, capital-disciplined, and deliberately conservative about Q4 noise.

44% reported core-Celsius growth off a depressed base implies a meaningful negative delta vs the 13% measured-channel growth when adding back $110-120M to the base - explain the wide variance and whether the add-back should have been lower.

Yes, with many puts and takes; over 52 weeks mix, promos and timing change, Q2 benefited from Prime Day buildup that occurred in early Q3; inventory-optimization add-back was a lower number, not a perfect one-to-one; 13% scanner is the good barometer; October running ahead of category growth; Live Fit Go campaign building trial ahead of 2026 resets.
How is management thinking about price points across Celsius, Alani Nu and Rockstar given Monster's announced pricing, and is Q4 messy before normalizing in Q1?

Pricing a hot topic given tariff/commodity headwinds; contemplating frontline price and promotional strategies and building a revenue-management team, no announcement; Q4 activity concentrated in December; unlike the 2022 one-for-one Celsius swap, the Alani Nu roll-in is phased to align with resets, ramping across December into Q1; captaincy means not a one-for-one replacement.
Q4 transition noise & net inventory drag

Be more specific on the optimized warehouse/distribution effects on inventory, how much the intra-quarter transition mitigates Q4 disruption, where the noise nets out, and whether returns coming in could outpace pipeline refill.

Being transparent on Q4 puts and takes - year-end CPG cash management plus inventory build as Alani Nu enters the PepsiCo warehouse system; declined to throw out numbers ('really noisy'); picking up returns from the prior network (logistics, secondary warehousing), supply chain not yet integrated; a possible net drag 'could be a scenario that plays out' with the return pickup unknown; 250+ distributors involved.
Sequential inventory & Alani Nu growth durability

Did Pepsi inventories decline sequentially in Q3, and how to think about the going-forward Alani Nu growth rate for the core brand and incremental LTO contribution given scanner growth has slowed since Q2?

LTO lumpiness - Witch's Brew in its fifth year more than doubled; underlying distribution and TDP gains to be captured through 2026 as Alani Nu reaches Celsius-level ACV; Winter Wonderland smaller than Witch's Brew and not at full potential crossing the transition; on sequential inventory, declined further detail - 'that's really all we're going to go with'.
Gross margin puts and takes, tariffs, Midwest premium, hedging
Color on Q3 gross-margin puts and takes and the forward outlook, the tariff impact, the Midwest-premium inflation impact, and the hedging strategy.

Gross profit an opportunity area as Alani Nu and Rockstar integrate; Midwest premium a headwind; no long-term hedging (only forward buys), evaluating it as purchasing power grows; tariffs slight in Q2, more in Q3, larger in Q4, partly offset by scale, synergies and vertical integration; second copacker line in 2026; Rockstar margin improves H1 2026; Alani Nu margin capture mostly by end of Q1; freight (Celsius ~3% of sales) can come down.
International plans now that the company is deeper into Alani Nu ownership and has considered Rockstar, and how international performance has gone.

Significant international opportunity; first president of international expansion just hired; foundation built over several years (Sweden, Finland, then Australia, UK, Ireland, NZ, France, Benelux); leaning in for 2026 with strategic investments; Australia the most successful early market (7-Eleven leaned in); Celsius pushed first internationally with Alani Nu to follow - a growth driver for years.
Alani Nu distribution ramp & avoiding inventory-optimization repeat
Whether Alani Nu can reach Celsius-level ACV/TDP without repeating the 2024 inventory-optimization episode.

The same ACV and TDP opportunity that benefited Celsius lies within Alani Nu; ramp expected to be more of a quarterly transition over the next three to six months as the company works through 2026 planogram resets, capturing distribution gains in a measured way.
